title: sandhi plainly
hook: one Vedic verse chanted two ways, joined and unjoined, and the week's joins undone
tomorrow: why can't a dictionary find bhargo, from the Gayatri?

segments.voice: Yesterday, sandhi plainly: an a and an e folding into ai, and the whole earth inside one family. Today, the week from the top, and an old way of chanting with every join undone.

A slowed-down version of a song can do something the original can't: each word lands on its own, and a lyric misheard for years suddenly makes sense. The same verse of the Rig Veda can be chanted two ways. Once as it's usually heard, every word flowing into the next. And once more, slowly, each word set down alone, as if it had never met its neighbors. Tradition kept both. The second one has a name: padapatha, the recitation word by word.
screen: `A SONG, SLOWED DOWN.` → `ONE VERSE, CHANTED TWO WAYS.` → `PADAPATHA: WORD BY WORD.`

segments.voice: The joined chant is called the samhita, the putting together. The unjoined one is the padapatha, and in it the joins come undone. Run this week's words through the same undoing. Namaste goes back to namah and te. The Chandogya's line opens back into a choice the schools still read two ways. Karmany eva becomes karmani and eva. Jagannath gives back jagat. Vasudhaiva lets go of eva. For a learner, the padapatha is a gift: sandhi undone by people who knew the verse by heart, a key kept right beside the lock. And tradition says the reciters went further, chanting the words in patterns, in pairs, forward and back, so a single slip would be heard. The joins were taught by being undone, and done again, aloud. So, the week: a breath that turns into s. Two a's that melt and hide a choice. An i that becomes y. A t that gets ready for its neighbor. An a and an e that fold into ai. Each one a small, sensible movement of the mouth, written down. Each one able to be undone.
screen: `SAMHITA: THE PUTTING TOGETHER.` · `PADAPATHA: EVERY JOIN UNDONE.` · `IN PAIRS, FORWARD AND BACK.` · `THE WEEK'S JOINS, UNDONE.` · then, large: `EVERY JOIN CAN BE UNDONE.`

segments.voice: Close the eyes and take namaste apart, the padapatha way: namah, a pause, te. Then join it again. For the rest of the sit, let the breath do the same: a small pause at the end of each out-breath, and the next breath joining on.
Sandhi plainly: the joins between words, made by the mouth, and undone, word by word, in the padapatha.
The week's line: sandhi plainly, where every join can be undone and done again. Another week, walked.
